```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(eatPrep)

# Replay the documented decisions when building the vignette. The interactive
# function and its namespace remain unchanged; only this local copy uses a script.
review_example <- function(dat, info, decisions) {
  answers <- decisions
  env <- new.env(parent = environment(visualSubsetRecode))
  env$.subset_menu <- function(choices) {
    if (!length(answers)) stop("Missing example decision.")
    answer <- answers[1]
    answers <<- answers[-1]
    if (!answer %in% choices) stop("Unknown example decision: ", answer)
    answer
  }
  review <- visualSubsetRecode
  environment(review) <- env
  invisible(capture.output(
    result <- suppressMessages(review(dat, info, toRecodeVal = "mci"))
  ))
  stopifnot(length(answers) == 0L)
  result
}
```

A technical incident can affect one participant, a whole class, one item, or an
entire test block. With rotated booklets, the first block can contain different
items for different participants. `prepareSubsetInfo()` translates the incident
reports and test design into explicit person-item pairs. `visualSubsetRecode()`
then lets you inspect each incident and decide which of those responses to recode.

The workflow is: **describe incidents, resolve the affected cells, inspect the
selection, review the responses, and retain the results and decision history**.
No recoding takes place during preparation or `summary()`.

## Choose the point in the preparation pipeline

Start with merged response data containing one row per participant and one column
per subunit. You can review raw responses or responses already processed by
`recodeData()`. Review before aggregating subunits into items, while the columns
described by the design are still available. Aggregated item names are not inferred.

Choose a replacement code that fits the subsequent scoring and missing-value
rules. Here, `"mci"` marks responses invalidated because of an incident. A character
replacement can convert numeric response columns to character. All review actions
preserve existing `NA` values. Review before `collapseMissings()` if the distinction
between different missing-value codes is needed for your decisions.

`automateDataPreparation()` does not call this review automatically. Pause the
pipeline at the appropriate stage and pass the returned `$dat` to the subsequent
preparation steps. See [Main Functions](main_functions.html) for those steps.

## Example: a class incident and an individual report

Three participants answer four items. Participants P1 and P2 belong to class K1,
but use booklets with different block orders. Participant P3 belongs to class K2.

```{r responses-and-persons}
review_data <- data.frame(
  ID = c("P1", "P2", "P3"),
  I1 = c(1, 0, 1), I2 = c(0, 1, 0),
  I3 = c(1, 1, 0), I4 = c(0, NA, 1)
)
persons <- data.frame(
  ID = c("P1", "P2", "P3"), classId = c("K1", "K1", "K2")
)
review_data
```

The design tables use the same structure as `inputList$booklets`,
`inputList$blocks`, and `inputList$rotation`:

```{r design}
booklets <- data.frame(
  booklet = c("X", "Y"), block1 = c("A", "B"), block2 = c("B", "A")
)
blocks <- data.frame(
  subunit = c("I1", "I2", "I3", "I4"),
  block = c("A", "A", "B", "B"), subunitBlockPosition = c(1, 2, 1, 2)
)
rotation <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2", "P3"), booklet = c("X", "Y", "X"))
booklets
rotation
```

Suppose an audio failure affected **block position 1 in class K1**. There is also
an individual report about item I1 for P1. Record one row per incident:

```{r incidents}
issues <- data.frame(
  issueId = c("V1", "V2"), level = c("class", "person"),
  targetId = c("K1", "P1"), scope = c("blockPosition", "item"),
  target = c("1", "I1"), comment = c("Audio failure", "Display error")
)
issues
```

Each report needs a unique `issueId`. `level` specifies whether `targetId` names a
person or class. `scope` determines how `target` is interpreted:

| `scope` | Interpretation of `target` | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `item` | One subunit name, or its recoded column name | `"I1"` |
| `block` | One block name, wherever it occurs in each person's booklet | `"A"` |
| `blockPosition` | One positive integer position in each person's booklet | `"1"` |

A report currently selects one target. Use additional rows with separate incident
IDs for additional targets. `comment` is optional and may contain `NA`. Class IDs
must identify classes across the whole data set; combine school and class IDs
beforehand if class names repeat between schools.

## Resolve and inspect the selection

```{r prepare}
subset_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(
  review_data, issues, persons = persons,
  booklets = booklets, blocks = blocks, rotation = rotation
)
subset_info[c("issueId", "ID", "datCols", "block", "blockPosition")]
summary(subset_info)
```

V1 selects **P1/I1, P1/I2, P2/I3, and P2/I4**. P1 uses block A first; P2 uses
block B first. P3 is outside the affected class. V2 independently selects P1/I1,
so that cell appears once for each incident.

The summary counts persons, distinct items, selected cells, and cells also
selected by another incident. V1 has four cells, including the missing response
P2/I4, and one overlapping cell. V2 has one cell, which overlaps with V1. Counts
refer to the proposed selection, not to completed recodings.

A named block gives a different selection. For example, block A occurs at
position 1 for P1 and position 2 for P2:

```{r named-block}
block_issue <- issues[1, ]
block_issue$scope <- "block"
block_issue$target <- "A"
block_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(
  review_data, block_issue, persons = persons,
  booklets = booklets, blocks = blocks, rotation = rotation
)
block_info[c("ID", "datCols", "blockPosition")]
```

Preparation stops on unknown classes, class members absent from `dat`, unresolved
item columns, and targets absent from a person's booklet. Correct the reports or
design before reviewing; affected persons are never silently omitted. Item-only
reports can omit all three design tables. When the tables are supplied, item
selections are also checked against each person's booklet.

## Review the responses

Run the following call in an interactive R session:

```{r interactive-review, eval=FALSE}
result <- visualSubsetRecode(review_data, subset_info, toRecodeVal = "mci")
```

Prepared selections automatically group the review by `issueId`, use the stored
person-ID column, show comments, and enable positions when all positions are
available. Persons with the same selected item layout are displayed together.
The console also reports overlaps and counts the selected values, including NAs.

For this first pass, choose **yes, all values** for V1, **no** for V2, and **yes**
when asked whether to end the review. The rendered example replays those decisions
without opening interactive menus, using the same recoding function.

```{r replay-first-pass, include=FALSE}
result <- review_example(review_data, subset_info, c("yes, all values", "no", "yes"))
```

```{r reviewed-data}
result$dat
```

P1/I1, P1/I2, and P2/I3 now contain `"mci"`. P2/I4 remains `NA`. P1/I3, P1/I4,
P2/I1, P2/I2, and all of P3's responses retain their original values. Only the
selected person-item pairs can change; selecting several people does not select
all combinations of their items.

The menus offer these decisions:

| Decision | Effect |
|---|---|
| All values | Recode selected cells whose original values are not NA. |
| All non-valid values | Recode selected cells originally containing `-99`, `-98`, `-97`, or `-96`. |
| Specific blocks | Choose among the actual block positions in the current selection; offered when positions are available. |
| No / flag for later review | Leave the current recoding selection unchanged. Flags are recorded but are not revisited automatically. |
| Go back | Return to the previous incident. |
| Reset to original values | Withdraw this incident's recoding selection; retain changes still selected by another incident. |
| Exit | Return completed changes after confirming exit. |

A new recoding action replaces that incident's earlier selection. Filters for
non-valid values use the original input responses, even if a previous decision
has already changed the displayed values. The replacement code is the same for
all incidents in one call. The block submenu selects positions, so position 1
can again refer to different named blocks for different people.

## Overlaps and reset

Each incident owns its selection. A cell remains recoded while any incident still
selects it; there is no automatic priority between class and individual reports.
To see the effect, start again with the original `review_data` and make these
decisions:

| Step | Current prompt | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | V1 | Yes, all values |
| 2 | V2 | Yes, all values |
| 3 | End review? | Go back |
| 4 | V2 | Go back to previous subset |
| 5 | V1 | Reset to original values |
| 6 | V2 | No |
| 7 | End review? | Yes |

```{r replay-reset, include=FALSE}
reset_result <- review_example(review_data, subset_info, c(
  "yes, all values", "yes, all values", "go back",
  "go back to previous subset", "reset to original values", "no", "yes"
))
```

```{r reset-data}
reset_result$dat
```

Only P1/I1 remains `"mci"`, because V2 still selects it. The changes to P1/I2 and
P2/I3 are withdrawn with V1's reset. Choosing **no** for V2 leaves its earlier
selection intact. To withdraw that selection too, reset V2 explicitly.

## Interpret and retain the results

The return value has two components: `$dat` contains the modified response data;
`$subsetInfo` joins reviewed selection rows to the decision history. Positional
access through `[[1]]` and `[[2]]` remains available.

```{r history}
unique(reset_result$subsetInfo[c("issueId", "choice", "timeStamp")])
```

Repeated reviews create multiple history entries. This table is not a final-status
table or a complete cell-level change log. In particular, the history records the
block-submenu action but does not store which block positions were chosen.
Unreviewed incidents are absent. Keep the original data, incident reports,
prepared selection, replacement code, and returned result together. For example:

```{r save-results, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(list(
  original = review_data, issues = issues, persons = persons,
  booklets = booklets, blocks = blocks, rotation = rotation,
  selection = subset_info, replacement = "mci", result = result
), "subset_review.rds")
```

Use the differences between original and returned data if you need a list of
final cell changes. Saving the result preserves completed work; it does not create
a resumable review session. Normal exit returns completed changes, but interrupt
recovery and automatic resumption are not implemented.

## Use project metadata and recoded columns

In a project, the design tables can come directly from `inputList`. After
`recodeData()`, also supply `inputList$subunits` to map original `subunit` names
to `subunitRecoded` column names:

```{r project-inputs, eval=FALSE}
dat_for_review <- recodeData(
  merged_data, values = inputList$values, subunits = inputList$subunits
)
selection <- prepareSubsetInfo(
  dat_for_review, issues, persons = persons,
  booklets = inputList$booklets, blocks = inputList$blocks,
  rotation = inputList$rotation, subunits = inputList$subunits
)
reviewed <- visualSubsetRecode(dat_for_review, selection, toRecodeVal = "mci")
dat_for_next_step <- reviewed$dat
```

Each selected subunit must resolve to exactly one response column. Supplying both
the original and recoded column for a selected subunit is ambiguous and produces
an error. Class membership comes separately from `persons`. For other identifier
column names, set `ID` and `classID` in `prepareSubsetInfo()`; the prepared object
retains the person-ID column name for the review.

Large numeric identifiers are kept distinct throughout preparation, display, and
recoding, while the returned response data retain their original ID type:

```{r large-identifiers}
large_data <- review_data
large_data$ID <- 1e15 + 1:3
large_issue <- data.frame(
  issueId = "large-id", level = "person", targetId = "1000000000000002",
  scope = "item", target = "I3"
)
large_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(large_data, large_issue)
large_info[c("ID", "datCols")]
```

Import identifiers as character if leading zeros or digits beyond numeric
precision must be preserved. Converting to character after import cannot recover
digits already lost. Character identifiers are matched exactly.

Existing manually prepared tables with person ID and `datCols` remain accepted.
For these tables, specify `useGroups`, `positions`, and `comments` explicitly when
needed. Explicit person exceptions and different replacement values per incident
are not available in the prepared-incident workflow.
